Why do earbuds and micro-usb cables seem to stop working after just 1-3 months?

TL;DR Because you buy cheap shit.

MicroUSB: wire gauge is very important. Think about all the other electronics in your house. Does anything have a power cable as skinny as your USB cables? All cables are not equal and you didn't get an "amazing deal" on that cable you bought for just $2. Inside every MicroUSB cable is a copper wire. Each gauge has a different capacity. Cheaper cables are just that, cheaper. To cut costs they contain less copper and those thin copper wires are being expected to pull more and more power to charge your shit. As might be expected, thin cable+ more power= dead cable.

Headphones/Ear buds: same as the above plus unskilled Chinese labourers fucking up solder points/using inadequate solder leads to high failure rates with extended use/manipulation of the cables. Every electronic device you purchase, unless very clear marked otherwise, is manufactured in China by an army of wage slaves. Unless you buy premium, you're still buying the same crap. You need to do research. Look at reviews and check into each manufacturer's policies.
